Located in the Milky Way roughly 1,600 light-years away from Earth in the constellation Virgo, the white dwarf is designated as J13281450. Astronomers made the observations utilizing the European Southern Observatory’s Very Large Telescope situated in Chile.

This discovery marks a departure from previous findings. Prior to this observation, astronomers had identified 21 white dwarfs with surrounding planetary debris, and all of them featured only a single disc. Researchers believe the newly observed double ring structure was likely shaped by two planetary or smaller rocky bodies that managed to survive the violent death throes of the star.

The white dwarf possesses a mass approximately 47 percent that of the sun, packed into a diameter roughly equal to that of Earth. A white dwarf represents the dense core left behind after a sun-like star runs out of fuel, expands into a red giant, and sheds its outer layers at the end of its life cycle.

This finding offers valuable insights into stellar evolution and potential outcomes for our own solar system billions of years in the future when the sun eventually exhausts its fuel. According to study co-author Felipe Lagos-Vilches of Universidad Tecnica Federico Santa Maria in Chile, the discovery proves that planetary system remnants can possess complex structures and confirms that rocky bodies can survive a star's transformation.

stories.title: British Pakistani Woman Alleges Courtroom Harassment by Ex-Husband in Lahore
stories.summary:
A British Pakistani woman named Laleen has filed a police application alleging harassment and intimidation by her former husband on the premises of the Lahore sessions court. The complainant visited the court for a maintenance hearing regarding their three daughters. Although she obtained a Khula and custody of the children years ago, she claimed her ex-husband and unidentified individuals confronted her, hurled verbal abuse, and issued death threats inside the judge's chamber.

According to the complaint submitted on October 23, the businessman ex-husband shoved her and prevented her from contacting the police helpline. Despite providing video evidence, she stated that Islampura police were reluctant to register a case, though an inquiry officer noted that no cognisable offence was found after investigation. Laleen has appealed to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz for support and requested the removal of her youngest daughter's name from the Exit Control List.

The legal dispute involves a family court decree from January 2017 ordering the father to pay Rs100,000 monthly maintenance per child, plus educational expenses with an annual increase. The father challenged the amount as excessive, but the Lahore High Court dismissed his appeal. The high court ruled that a father cannot evade financial obligations or reduce the children's standard of living, emphasizing that maintenance must match his financial standing.

Despite the favorable ruling, execution proceedings remain pending, meaning the children have yet to receive their maintenance. The Lahore High Court recently underscored a wider systemic issue regarding prolonged enforcement proceedings, noting that delays at the execution stage defeat the purpose of adjudication and reduce court judgments to mere paper declarations.

stories.title: Sindh Chief Minister Declares Tharparkar District Drought-Hit
stories.summary:
Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah officially declared Tharparkar a drought-affected district on Saturday after reviewing severe agricultural losses and dry conditions across all seven talukas. During a meeting at the CM House in Karachi, officials reported that between 85 and 90 percent of cultivated crops have been destroyed or rendered unproductive due to uneven monsoon rainfall and very low precipitation in September.

The meeting included key figures such as MNA Dr Mahesh Malani, several MPAs, Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah, and other senior revenue and district officials. Attendees evaluated the extensive damage to agriculture, natural grass, and local livelihoods, noting that only 10 to 15 percent of crops managed to survive the harsh dry spell.

In response to the crisis, the chief minister ordered immediate relief efforts with a strong emphasis on protecting livestock, which serves as a primary source of income for residents of the desert region. He instructed authorities to repair non-functional reverse osmosis plants, resolve water supply issues, and examine the feasibility of constructing a dedicated water pipeline from Naukot to Mithi to secure long-term access to drinking water.

Furthermore, Mr Shah directed relevant departments to coordinate actions swiftly to address fodder shortages and distribute necessary aid. The provincial government pledged to remain vigilant and support local communities throughout the duration of the hardship.

stories.title: Chinese Giant Pandas Make Public Debut at Zoo Atlanta
stories.summary:
Two giant pandas on loan from China, a male named Ping Ping and a female named Fu Shuang, made their highly anticipated public debut at Zoo Atlanta on Friday. The pair delighted onlookers by lounging in their new habitat and chewing bamboo after arriving from Chengdu in September aboard a FedEx cargo flight known as the Panda Express. They are scheduled to stay at the southern US facility for the next ten years as part of Beijing's long-running diplomatic initiative.

Zoo CEO Raymond King highlighted the animals' unique ability to foster global connections and inspire joy during his remarks to visitors. Ahead of the arrival, the facility completed significant renovations to its panda habitat, established a dedicated team of caretakers, and secured a steady local supply of bamboo from Atlanta, a city chosen because its climate closely mirrors Chengdu's.

The public appearance of the pandas underscores the role of these black-and-white mammals in China's decades-long soft power strategy to build international ties. Native to temperate forests in East Asia, the animals are frequently shared with global zoos. This cultural display occurred as high-ranking American officials urged Beijing to respect trade commitments established during an October 2025 summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

The arrival of Ping Ping and Fu Shuang has generated considerable excitement among visitors, with many expressing how much happiness the animals bring. Zoo officials emphasized that the partnership with China creates a meaningful future for a species beloved worldwide. The exhibition serves as both a popular tourist attraction and a recurring symbol of international wildlife cooperation between the two nations.

stories.title: Houston Mayor Orders Police to Limit Immigration Enforcement Cooperation
stories.summary:
Houston Mayor John Whitmire directed the city's police department on Friday to scale back cooperation with federal immigration authorities. The decision follows recent state elections and aims to reduce anxiety among residents in Texas's most populous city. Mayor Whitmire stated that the policy shift was made after consulting with newly elected state leaders.

Under the updated directive, police officers conducting routine traffic stops or detaining individuals are prohibited from notifying US Immigration and Enforcement solely based on civil immigration warrants. Notification will only be permitted if the person is simultaneously arrested and facing a jailable criminal charge. Houston Police Chief J. Noe Diaz voiced his support for the policy, noting that implementation has already begun.

Mayor Whitmire, a Democrat who previously opposed the 2017 Texas statute banning sanctuary city policies during his time in the state Senate, described the order as a necessary step toward healing. He expressed hope that Houston's new framework could serve as a model for other municipalities across Texas.

The announcement comes shortly after the defeat of long-serving Republican Governor Greg Abbott in his bid for a fourth term, signaling a shifting political landscape in the state that emboldened local leaders to alter their approach to federal immigration enforcement.

stories.title: Egypt Reopens Embassy in Tripoli After Twelve Years
stories.summary:
Egypt officially reopened its embassy in the Libyan capital of Tripoli on Saturday, ending a twelve-year closure that began in 2014. The reopening marks a notable diplomatic shift for Cairo, which previously maintained strong ties with eastern-based military commander Khalifa Haftar amid Libya's long-standing political division.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty highlighted the historical importance of the embassy building during the reopening ceremony, emphasizing the deep cultural and human connections between Egypt and Libya. The diplomatic mission had shut its doors when numerous foreign embassies withdrew from Tripoli due to escalating conflicts that split the North African nation into rival administrations.

Libya has experienced persistent turmoil since the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that led to the fall of Muammar Qadhafi. The country remains politically divided between the eastern House of Representatives backed by the Libyan National Army under Khalifa Haftar and the eastern government led by Osama Hammad, alongside the internationally recognized Government of National Unity in the west headed by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah.

stories.title: New Delhi Ranks as World's Most Polluted Major City Prior to Diwali
stories.summary:
New Delhi was recorded as the world's most polluted major city on Saturday morning according to live rankings provided by the Swiss organization IQAir. The distressing air quality milestone arrived just one day before the Hindu festival of lights, Diwali, an occasion traditionally accompanied by widespread fireworks that further exacerbate regional smog.

In response to the escalating environmental hazard, Indian authorities ordered schools in and around the capital to transition to online learning and advised residents to work from home. IQAir placed Delhi at the top of its global index at 10:35 am with a US air quality index score of 581, which was twice the reading recorded in neighboring Lahore, Pakistan.

IQAir's measurements focus on specific pollutant concentrations and differ from India's domestic monitoring system. The Central Pollution Control Board reported Delhi's official air quality index at 363 during the morning hours, placing local air conditions firmly within the very poor category as residents braced for the holiday smog.

stories.title: Pakistan Reserves Ten Percent of Local LPG for State Companies
stories.summary:
A high-level committee in Islamabad decided that state-owned enterprises will receive a ten per cent allocation of locally produced liquefied petroleum gas, while private bidders in upcoming auctions will face a strict daily purchase cap of 20 tonnes. Meeting under the leadership of the petroleum secretary and with Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik present, the committee took steps to operationalize an auction framework previously approved by the federal cabinet on November 4.

Under the new guidelines, domestic producers must reserve a tenth of their output for public sector marketing companies to ensure stable supplies in remote and underserved regions. The remaining ninety per cent will be sold through transparent media-monitored auctions. State entities will pay the producer price tied to the Saudi Aramco FOB rate. The committee includes officials from the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority, state energy companies, and private sector representatives.

While the petroleum ministry stated that the 20-tonne restriction aims to create a fair and competitive playing field, industry associations strongly criticized the measure. The Pakistan LPG Marketers Association dismissed the auction plan as a superficial maneuver that fails to address the root cause of supply constraints, which they attribute to the closure of the border with Iran. Association representatives noted that local production covers only thirty per cent of national demand, meaning the public sector allocation equates to a modest 210 tonnes daily out of a 7,000-tonne market.

Industry leaders warned that the bidding process will likely drive prices higher and consolidate market control among financially powerful firms. Instead of the new framework, the marketers urged the government to slash import sales taxes, remove withholding taxes, and reduce port and terminal charges to make gas more affordable for ordinary consumers.

stories.title: Information Technology Earnings Propel Pakistani Services Exports Higher
stories.summary:
Pakistan's services exports achieved a strong year-on-year increase of 22.60 per cent during the first quarter of the 2026-27 fiscal year, propelled primarily by robust revenues from the information technology sector. According to official figures released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, total export proceeds reached $2.72 billion between July and September, climbing from $2.22 billion during the same period in the previous year.

In September alone, outbound shipments of services expanded by 15.35 per cent to $929.87 million, up from $806.14 million a year earlier. Telecommunication, computer, and information services remained the primary drivers of this financial expansion. State Bank of Pakistan data indicates that tech-related exports totaled $1.246 billion in the opening quarter of the fiscal year, marking a 17.7 per cent rise compared to the $1.059 billion recorded in the corresponding months of the prior year. Additional business services and transport sectors also registered growth of 27.98 per cent and 9.66 per cent, respectively.

Conversely, services imports experienced an upward trajectory as well, surging 16.32 per cent to $3.55 billion in the first quarter of 2026-27 compared to $3.05 billion previously. September imports climbed more sharply by 26.38 per cent to $1.21 billion. The transport and travel sectors accounted for the largest share of these incoming expenditures during the quarter.

Despite the rise in imports, the services trade deficit remained relatively stable at $832.16 million for the July-September quarter, showing a slight contraction of 0.33 per cent from the $834.88 million deficit recorded last year. However, the monthly deficit for September widened significantly by 84 per cent to reach $282.76 million on a year-on-year basis.

stories.title: Global Food Commodity Prices Ease in October Following Lower Demand
stories.summary:
International food commodity prices declined in October as subdued import demand led to lower price indices for cereals, dairy items, and meat. The benchmark Food Price Index, compiled by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation, averaged 133.9 points during the month, representing a decrease of 1.6 points or 1.2 per cent from its revised September level. Despite this monthly drop, the index remained 5.9 per cent higher than the same period a year ago, though it sits 16.4 per cent below its peak in March 2022.

The recent monthly decrease was driven largely by falling cereal quotations, particularly wheat, which dropped after four consecutive months of increases due to sluggish international demand and a more favorable production outlook. However, ongoing logistical challenges in the Black Sea region helped cushion the decline. While most commodity groups saw reductions, sugar prices experienced a sharp increase, and vegetable oils registered a marginal gain.

In a companion briefing on cereal supply and demand, the FAO forecast that global cereal production for 2026 will recede from the record set in 2025, while remaining the second-highest output on record at 2,999 million tonnes. Production is expected to contract across major crops, led by wheat, while rice output is projected to fall by 2.5 per cent to 552 million tonnes due to poor producer profit margins and weather patterns associated with El Niño.

Global cereal utilization for the 2026-27 period is anticipated to inch up by 0.2 per cent to 2,971 million tonnes, driven primarily by food consumption increases for wheat and rice. Meanwhile, worldwide cereal stocks are projected to grow by 1.8 per cent to close at higher inventory levels by 2027, largely reflecting accumulated wheat supplies in Russia and Ukraine where exports face ongoing bottlenecks.

stories.title: SECP Investigates Proposed IPO and Requests Bank Records
stories.summary:
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan has requested export records from seven banks as part of its ongoing inquiry into the proposed initial public offering of SE Fruits and Vegetable Limited, previously known as Shaheen Enterprises. In addition, the financial regulator has asked 30 banks to provide information regarding foreign remittances, export proceeds, and other foreign exchange transactions linked to the company's sponsors and directors. Some banks have already submitted their replies, which are currently being evaluated.

The regulatory investigation was officially launched on October 21 under Section 29 of the SECP Act 1997, combined with Section 139 of the Securities Act. Authorities are also reviewing details provided by the IPO's joint lead managers, Topline Securities and Growth Securities, alongside a submitted response from consultant Parker Russell-A.J.S. The investigative team is carefully checking the IPO application, shareholder information, and transfer histories.

The Central Depository Company provided a list of investors, prompting the regulator to seek relevant shareholder lists and transfer histories. A partial response from the Central Depository Company arrived on November 2 and is under review, while the company's auditor, Ilyas Saeed & Co, received an approved extension to submit its requested documents.

Prior to the inquiry, SE Fruits intended to raise up to Rs1.2 billion by offering 30 million shares at a price of Rs40 each. However, the regulatory body halted the public offering last month, leading the firm to withdraw the plan entirely. The ongoing probe matters because it oversees market compliance and protects investor interests in Pakistan's financial sectors.

stories.title: Heavy Rain Floods Thousands of Tents and Triggers Disasters Across Gaza
stories.summary:
Severe rainfall struck the war-torn Gaza Strip on Saturday, flooding tens of thousands of makeshift dwellings and leaving numerous displaced individuals completely without shelter. According to the Hamas-run government media office, approximately 70,000 tents housing thousands of people were inundated on the initial day of downpours. The extreme weather additionally caused cracked walls and roofs to collapse in various parts of the enclave, resulting in several injuries, some of which were critical.

Mahmoud Bassal, a civil defence spokesman, reported that his agency handled over 1,500 overnight calls from desperate residents seeking assistance due to flooded tents. He stressed that the civil defence unit operates entirely without necessary equipment or operational capabilities. A coalition of local Palestinian civil society organizations issued urgent pleas for international intervention, highlighting severe risks of epidemic and disease outbreaks while demanding that Israel lift restrictions on humanitarian aid entries.

Despite a fragile ceasefire that began on October 10, 2025, following two years of conflict and mediated by the United States, Qatar, and Egypt, Israeli military air strikes and ground operations have persisted nearly every day. Mustafa Qazzaat, a Gaza city council member and emergency committee official, noted that authorities never permitted prefabricated housing into the territory after the truce announcement, allowing only limited numbers of tents.

Qazzaat emphasized that the enclave urgently requires 200,000 prefabricated housing units alongside heavy machinery. Such equipment is vital for clearing rubble from demolished buildings, reopening primary roads, and restoring essential electricity and heating to the devastated population.

stories.title: انڈر 19 ایشیا کپ میں روایتی حریف پاکستان اور بھارت کا اہم میچ جاری
stories.summary:
عمان میں کھیلے جانے والے انڈر 19 ایشیا کپ کے ایک اہم اور دلچسپ میچ میں بھارت کی ٹیم کی جانب سے پاکستان کے خلاف بیٹنگ کا سلسلہ جاری ہے۔ اس میچ کے دوران بھارتی ٹیم نے اب تک پانچ وکٹوں کے نقصان پر چھیاسی (86) رنز بنا لیے ہیں۔ ٹورنامنٹ کے اس مرحلے پر دونوں ٹیمیں میدان میں آمنے سامنے ہیں۔

یاد رہے کہ اس ٹورنامنٹ کے گروپ اے میں پاکستان اور بھارت دونوں ہی اپنی مہم کا آغاز کرتے ہوئے اپنے اپنے ابتدائی میچز جیتنے میں کامیاب رہے تھے۔ جبکہ دوسری جانب گروپ بی میں افغانستان کی ٹیم اپنے کھیلے گئے تین میں سے دو میچوں میں فتح حاصل کر چکی ہے۔ میچ کے آغاز پر بھارت انڈر 19 ٹیم نے ٹاس جیتنے کے بعد خود پہلے بیٹنگ کرنے کا فیصلہ کیا تھا۔

اس ٹورنامنٹ کے قوانین کے مطابق گروپ اے اور گروپ بی میں سے دو، دو بہترین ٹیمیں اگلے راؤنڈ کے لیے کوالیفائی کریں گی۔ یہ بات بھی قابلِ ذکر ہے کہ اس سے پچھلے سیزن میں پاکستان نے شاندار کارکردگی کا مظاہرہ کرتے ہوئے فائنل کے معرکے میں بھارت کو ایک سو اکیانوے (191) رنز کے بڑے مارجن سے شکست دی تھی۔

stories.title: Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton Advance to Paris Masters Final
stories.summary:
Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have advanced to the Paris Masters final following contrasting victories in their respective semi-final matches. Alcaraz delivered a controlled performance to defeat former world number two Casper Ruud 6-4, 6-4, securing a straight-sets win without needing the dramatic heroics of his previous round against Taylor Fritz. 

Meanwhile, third seed Ben Shelton overcame a sluggish start to halt the impressive tournament run of French world number 47 Luca Van Assche 5-7, 6-3, 6-4. Despite committing a significant number of unforced errors in the opening set and conceding his serve in the 11th game, Shelton raised his level in the second and third sets to book his place in his sixth final of the season.

Sunday's championship match marks the first meeting between Alcaraz and Shelton since the latter ended Alcaraz's US Open title defense in the quarter-finals earlier in the season. Shelton enters the clash seeking his third Masters-level title, having won the previous two editions of the Canadian Open.

For Alcaraz, the victory marks his first-ever final appearance in Paris. Both players expressed enthusiasm for the upcoming title showdown, highlighting the excitement of competing against top-tier opponents late in the tennis season.

stories.title: Liam Delap Double Deepens Manchester City's Premier League Woes
stories.summary:
Manchester City suffered a third consecutive Premier League defeat after falling 3-1 to Nottingham Forest at the City Ground. Liam Delap starred for the hosts with a decisive double that lifted Forest out of the relegation zone and secured only their second win of the campaign.

Oliver Glasner's side capitalized on early defensive errors from City, with Jair Cunha opening the scoring after robbing Josko Gvardiol, followed shortly by Delap's first-half strike. Although Rayan Cherki gave City hope with a stunning goal early in the second half following a double substitution by manager Enzo Maresca, Forest sealed the victory 15 minutes from time when Morgan Gibbs-White fed Delap for a brilliant left-footed finish.

The defeat leaves Manchester City six points behind league leaders Arsenal. The club is currently grappling with uncertainty as they face a potential severe points deduction after being found guilty of over 100 Premier League financial rule charges, an issue pending appeal.

Maresca admitted his team failed to match the required match intensity during a poor first-half performance. Meanwhile, the result dropped Manchester United into the relegation zone ahead of their upcoming fixture against Aston Villa.

stories.title: مارشل عبدالرشید دوستم نے افغان طالبان رجیم کے خاتمے کی پیشگوئی کر دی
stories.summary:
افغان نیشنل موومنٹ پارٹی کے سربراہ اور سابق نائب صدر مارشل عبدالرشید دوستم نے افغان طالبان رجیم کے مستقبل پر سخت سوالات اٹھاتے ہوئے کہا ہے کہ یہ نام نہاد امارت زیادہ دیر برقرار نہیں رہ سکے گی اور بالآخر اپنے انجام کو پہنچ کر رہے گی۔

مارشل دوستم کا کہنا ہے کہ افغان عوام آزادی کی خاطر اپنی جانیں قربان کرنے والے شہداء کی قربانیوں کو کبھی فراموش نہیں کریں گے۔ انہوں نے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ ملک کے باشعور اور اعلیٰ تعلیم یافتہ نوجوان آزادی کے لیے شہداء کے مشن کو آگے بڑھا رہے ہیں۔

سابق نائب صدر نے مزید واضح کیا کہ یہی اعلیٰ تعلیم یافتہ افغان نوجوان مستقبل میں افغانستان کی تقدیر کا فیصلہ کریں گے۔ ان کے مطابق، طالبان رجیم کے خلاف مزاحمت بڑھ رہی ہے اور یہ حکومت اپنے انجام تک ضرور پہنچے گی۔

stories.title: Real Madrid Defeats Valencia 3-0 as Spanish Football Honors De Miguel
stories.summary:
Real Madrid secured a comfortable 3-0 victory away against Valencia, drawing level with La Liga leaders Barcelona. First-half goals from Federico Valverde and Arda Guler put Jose Mourinho's side in control at the Mestalla stadium, before Kylian Mbappe added a third in the second half to score in his seventh consecutive match for the club.

The match took place against the backdrop of nationwide tributes across Spanish football for Jesus de Miguel. The Tenerife striker tragically passed away following a collision with Andorra's goalkeeper in a second-division fixture, prompting matches across the country to feature a minute of silence and a minute of applause in the ninth minute to honor his shirt number.

Real Madrid dominated the encounter despite missing suspended winger Vinicius Junior for the final match of his four-match ban. Valencia's evening worsened late in the game when captain Jose Gaya received a red card for a sliding foul on Mbappe, leaving Los Che 19th in the standings and a point from safety.

Mourinho praised his team's emotional balance following their winning run, noting that the squad maintained composure after their last defeat against Atletico Madrid in September. Reigning champions Barcelona are set to face Atletico Madrid next.

stories.title: بھارت میں مودی حکومت کی آمرانہ پالیسیوں کیخلاف خانہ جنگی کا خدشہ ظاہر
stories.summary:
بھارت میں بڑھتی ہوئی سیاسی و عوامی مخالفت نے موجودہ مودی حکومت کے جابرانہ رویے اور آمرانہ پالیسیوں کو بری طرح بے نقاب کر دیا ہے۔ ریاست جھارکھنڈ کے صحت کے وزیر ڈاکٹر عرفان انصاری نے 40 لاکھ طلبہ کے جاری احتجاج کو عوام کی شدید بے چینی کا واضح ثبوت قرار دیا ہے۔

بھارتی جریدے ٹائمز آف انڈیا کی رپورٹس کے مطابق، نااہل مودی حکومت کی پالیسیاں ملک کے کسانوں، نوجوانوں اور اقلیتوں سمیت تمام طبقات کے لیے معاشی اور سماجی استحصال کا سبب بن رہی ہیں۔ حکمران طبقہ عوامی مفاد کو مکمل طور پر پسِ پشت ڈال کر مسلسل عوام دشمن اقدامات کو فروغ دے رہا ہے۔

عوام میں روز بروز بڑھتا ہوا یہ شدید غصہ اس بات کو ہوا دے رہا ہے کہ بھارت میں بنگلہ دیش اور نیپال سے بھی بڑی خانہ جنگی یا شدید نوعیت کا داخلی تصادم جنم لے سکتا ہے۔

stories.title: Zabarnyi Header Secures Narrow Victory for PSG Against Troyes
stories.summary:
Paris Saint-Germain secured a narrow 1-0 victory against Troyes in Ligue 1 on Saturday, marking their 11th consecutive win across all competitions under coach Luis Enrique. Ukraine defender Illia Zabarnyi scored the game's only goal with a header in the 39th minute following a quickly taken corner by Desire Doue and a cross from Senny Mayulu. The win brought PSG three points clear at the top of the table.

PSG played without several key players, as Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembele, Nuno Mendes, Maghnes Akliouche, and captain Marquinhos were injured, while Achraf Hakimi was rested and Joao Neves began on the bench. Despite the depleted squad and a dogged performance from the newly promoted Troyes side backed by the City Football Group, Luis Enrique's team maintained their winning momentum following a midweek Champions League victory over Villarreal.

During the match, Spain's Ferran Torres missed several scoring chances, extending his scoreless streak to eight games. Troyes also threatened when Renaud Ripart missed a clear opportunity and Lucas Maronnier had a late goal disallowed for offside. PSG fans also ignited fireworks during the second half of the fixture at the Parc des Princes.

Following the international break, PSG will face Nice away before hosting Roma in the Champions League. In other league action on Saturday, Paris FC defeated Auxerre 1-0 with a goal from Lassine Sinayoko, moving them into second place behind PSG. Meanwhile, Lens prepared to face Marseille following a record-equalling 9-1 Champions League defeat against Como.

stories.title: Heavy Rain Floods Gaza Tents as Emergency Services Face Shortages
stories.summary:
Heavy rain and strong winds flooded 70,000 tents across the Gaza Strip starting late Friday, leaving displaced Palestinian families without proper shelter. According to the Government Media Office, the severe weather also brought down dozens of walls and caused initial losses estimated at approximately $3 million. Medical sources reported that five Palestinians sustained injuries from collapsing walls and falling corrugated metal sheets damaged by previous Israeli strikes.

Gaza Municipality spokesman Hosni Muhanna stated that about one million residents and displaced individuals are crowded into roughly 30 percent of Gaza City, straining infrastructure heavily damaged by war. The city recorded 60 millimeters of rain in 12 hours, amounting to about 15 percent of its annual rainfall. Municipal crews received 250 calls regarding flooded streets, erosion, and blocked drains, while warning that 270 camp and shelter sites faced flooding risks due to drainage capacity being reduced to 20 percent.

Abdullah al-Majdalawi, public relations director for Gaza's Civil Defense, reported hundreds of distress calls concerning flooded tents and collapsing structures. Responders faced entire camps submerged with tents, bedding, and furniture, but lacked the resources to provide alternative housing for the displaced population. Officials blamed the lack of safer alternatives on ongoing blockades and restrictions regarding reconstruction materials and mobile homes.

Data from UNRWA indicated that 1.98 million people, representing 94 percent of Gaza's population, required shelter and essential supplies, with 58 percent facing critical or catastrophic needs. The ongoing crisis stems from widespread destruction caused by the conflict that began in October 2023, with reconstruction efforts continuously hampered by severe material restrictions.

stories.title: Lionel Messi Secures Second Consecutive MLS Golden Boot Award
stories.summary:
Inter Miami's Lionel Messi won his second straight MLS Golden Boot award on Saturday, despite his team settling for a 3-3 draw against Charlotte on the final day of the regular season. Messi did not score in the match at Miami's Nu Stadium but provided two assists from corner kicks in the first half. The result helped secure a home-field advantage for Inter Miami in the first two rounds of the upcoming playoffs.

Messi finished the season with 26 goals, making him the first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boot awards. Dallas player Petar Musa finished second in the scoring race with 22 goals after remaining scoreless in a 3-1 victory over Colorado. Inter Miami's early goals against Charlotte came from Ian Fray, Luis Suarez, and Rodrigo De Paul, before Liel Abada scored twice and Rodolfo Aloko equalized in the 90th minute for Charlotte.

In the wider league standings, Nashville set a new all-time MLS points record by finishing with 77 points after defeating Cincinnati 2-0 to claim the top spot in the Eastern Conference. Inter Miami finished second in the East with 60 points, while New England placed third with 58 points following a loss to Orlando. Inter Miami will face Columbus in the opening round of the Eastern Conference playoffs.

In the Western Conference, champions Vancouver defeated Montreal 2-0 to finish second overall. Decision Day matches also determined the final playoff berths and matchups, with Portland, Seattle, and Real Salt Lake securing postseason spots alongside conference leaders amidst a full slate of league fixtures.

stories.title: How the Consensus Rule Became a Veto on Climate Action
stories.summary:
Delegates gathering at the Antalya Expo Centre for the UN climate talks face a long-standing structural flaw where single governments or small coalitions can block agreements. The system relies entirely on consensus to give every nation a voice, but the absence of an agreed voting mechanism for stalemates grants opponents of climate action the power to halt progress. Dr Joanna Depledge, a research fellow at Cambridge, notes that the root of the problem dates back to the 1995 Berlin COP when draft rules proposing a two-thirds majority vote as a last resort were successfully blocked by OPEC members including Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.

This procedural dispute left climate negotiations without a voting rule for substantive decisions. Depledge describes the resistance as a deliberate strategy heavily influenced by fossil-fuel interests, where opponents find it easier to reject agreements than to negotiate compromises. This approach has manifested through delaying tactics, outright refusals, and exploiting mistrust between developed nations and the Global South over historical emissions and financial obligations. While petrostates have driven much of this obstruction, they have occasionally found alignment with major emerging economies like China and India, who share concerns regarding potential new mitigation mandates and the protection of national sovereignty.

Defenders of consensus, such as Saudi Arabia, the Arab Group, and the Like-Minded Developing Countries, argue that majority voting threatens national sovereignty and risks allowing wealthy nations to rewrite historical responsibilities or impose unfair conditions on climate finance. They contend that decisions forced over a country's formal objection lack legitimacy and implementation support. However, critics point out that the consensus model has allowed opposing nations to stall vital discussions on sectors like aviation and fossil fuels for decades, creating a system where the pace of global climate policy is dictated by the least ambitious participants.

stories.title: Reflecting on the Centenary and Legacy of Legendary Singer Noor Jahan
stories.summary:
The centenary of legendary playback singer Madam Noor Jahan passed with minimal official recognition, highlighting a societal tendency to overlook cultural icons. Born Allah Rakhi Wasai on September 21, 1925, in Kasur, she came from a family deeply rooted in music. Encouraged by her family, she began formal training in classical vocalization at just five years old under masters like Ustad Ghulam Muhammad and Kajjanbai, mastering ragas and expanding her vocal range.

Her career began on stage with a rural theatre troupe before moving to Calcutta in the 1930s under the mentorship of Mukhtar Begum, adopting the stage name Baby Noor Jahan. She appeared as a child actor in Punjabi films such as *Pind di Kuri* (1935), *Missar Ka Sitara* (1936), and *Heer Sayyal* (1937). Relocating to Lahore in 1938, she transitioned to adult roles, achieving massive commercial success and national fame with the 1942 film *Khandaan*, directed by Shaukat Hussain Rizvi, whom she married in 1943.

Following her move to Bombay, Noor Jahan became a top-grossing star with blockbusters like *Badi Ma* (1945), *Zeenat* (1945), and *Jugnu* (1947). After the Partition of India, she and Rizvi settled in Karachi, Pakistan. In 1951, she co-directed and starred in *Chanwey*, becoming Pakistan's first female film director, and followed it with another hit, *Dupatta* (1952).

Over a six-decade career, Noor Jahan stood out for her refusal to lip-sync in pre-recorded studio settings, instead delivering raw, authentic performances that captivated audiences. Despite her monumental contributions to South Asian music and cinema, her legacy faces the threat of being overshadowed by scandals and rumors surrounding her private life. Observers argue that celebrating her life requires focusing on fact-based accounts of her artistic achievements rather than sensationalized narratives.

Ultimately, remembering luminaries like Noor Jahan is vital for preserving the rich cultural history of the subcontinent. As her 26th death anniversary approaches, promoting accurate documentation of her work ensures that future generations appreciate her enduring musical brilliance and unflagging commitment to her craft, protecting her memory from fading into obscurity.

stories.title: British-Pakistani Entrepreneur Honors Jinnah Through Business and Philanthropy
stories.summary:
Saleem Akhtar, a British-Pakistani entrepreneur based in Bradford, has built a life and career that continuously honors Pakistan's founder, Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah. Moving to the United Kingdom as a 10-year-old child, Akhtar has channeled his deep attachment to his homeland into commercial enterprise and humanitarian work. His restaurant group, named Jinnah, introduces traditional Kashmiri and Pakistani cuisine to customers across Yorkshire, using food as a vital bridge for cultural preservation.

The family's business journey in Britain began in 1981 with a modest shop, eventually expanding into the Jinnah restaurant group. A significant milestone occurred in 2015 with an investment exceeding £500,000 to open a restaurant at the historic Gate House building on Leeds Road in Bradford, creating 32 local jobs. For Akhtar, naming the business after Jinnah was a deliberate choice to keep the historical leader's legacy visible in a multicultural British city while educating younger generations of British Pakistanis about their heritage.

Akhtar's personal tribute extends to his vehicles, which exclusively feature Jinnah-themed number plates as a daily expression of gratitude and admiration. Beyond business and symbolism, he is heavily engaged in philanthropy supporting Pakistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). Following the devastating 2005 earthquake, his foundation distributed Rs 10 million in cash to affected individuals in Muzaffarabad and Bagh, and later constructed 20 houses for families displaced by the September 2019 earthquake in Mirpur.

Believing that expatriates should maintain tangible connections with their roots, Akhtar actively advocates for overseas Pakistanis to invest in their ancestral towns and villages. He argues that even modest economic investments can create lasting links, giving younger family members practical reasons to visit, engage with local communities, and better understand their family history.

Akhtar's story highlights the multifaceted nature of the overseas Pakistani experience, merging entrepreneurial drive with cultural preservation and philanthropy. By creating jobs, supporting vulnerable communities, and investing in local development, he demonstrates that physical distance from a homeland does not require emotional or cultural detachment, leaving a legacy that bridges two different worlds.

stories.title: Pope Leo Urges Uruguayan Youth to Value Family and Human Connection
stories.summary:
Pope Leo XIV encouraged young people to confront modern uncertainties with courage, prioritize real human relationships, and embrace marriage and family life. Speaking to a crowd of 70,000 people at Montevideo's historic Estadio Centenario during a prayer vigil, the pontiff cautioned against the rising isolation of the digital age. He warned that virtual interactions and screens cannot replace genuine human contact, urging youth to look into each other's eyes and share experiences face-to-face.

During a separate meeting with academics and students at the Catholic University of Uruguay, Pope Leo addressed the role of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. He stressed that educational institutions must guide students in using technology wisely while ensuring that human beings remain at the center of technological advancement, harmonizing technical, emotional, spiritual, and ecological intelligence.

The pontiff also visited the impoverished and crime-affected Casavalle neighborhood, stopping at the Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe Church. In a country rich in natural resources, he asserted that no child should suffer from hunger, lack a decent education, or face insecurity in the streets. Later, he held a major open-air mass in Paysandu for 40,000 faithful, where he embraced Uruguay's mate-drinking tradition as a symbol of regional solidarity, fraternity, and social bonding.

As part of his South American tour, Pope Leo's visit to Uruguay precedes his arrival in Argentina. Ahead of the papal visit, the Argentine government raised its security alert to the highest level, preparing an unprecedented security operation for the leader of the Catholic Church.

stories.title: England Fast Bowler Josh Tongue Ruled Out of Australia Tour
stories.summary:
England fast bowler Josh Tongue has been forced to withdraw from the team's white-ball tour of Australia due to a toe injury and will travel back home for medical care. The 28-year-old athlete arrived in Perth last week ahead of a schedule featuring three One Day Internationals and five Twenty20 matches, but he sat out during a 92-run one-day warm-up victory against Western Australia.

Team management confirmed that a left big toe injury sidelined Tongue, stating he will return to the United Kingdom for further medical evaluation. Batter Jacob Bethell also missed the warm-up match as he continues recovering from knee surgery, while teammates Jofra Archer and Adil Rashid delivered strong performances by taking 3-34 and 4-35 respectively to bowl Western Australia out for 159.

During the same fixture, Ben Duckett contributed 59 runs and Liam Dawson finished unbeaten on 44 as England secured the warm-up win. The touring squad is set to begin the ODI leg of the tour in Perth on Friday before travelling to subsequent matches in Adelaide and Hobart, marking England's initial return to Australia following a 4-1 defeat in the 2025-26 Ashes Test series.

stories.title: Former Test Opener Usman Khawaja Defends 2018 Ball-Tampering Claims
stories.summary:
Retired Australian batsman Usman Khawaja has strongly defended remarks in his upcoming autobiography asserting that the entire Australian cricket team was complicit in the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering plot. Khawaja insisted that his statements did not amount to throwing anyone under the bus, emphasizing instead that the entire squad shared collective responsibility for the incident.

Following the original scandal, Steve Smith, David Warner, and Cameron Bancroft faced heavy public humiliation and suspensions, while the rest of the team avoided formal punishment. Khawaja argued that these three individuals served as victims who absorbed the blame on behalf of everyone involved, noting that the tactic had previously been utilized during a Test match at Port Elizabeth.

Khawaja explained that he initially attempted to speak out in 2018, but Steve Smith personally persuaded him to stay silent to protect the team. He considered addressing the matter again in 2021 after several bowlers publicly denied prior knowledge, but ultimately chose to remain quiet following discussions with then-coach Justin Langer.

Cricket Australia stated it remains satisfied with its original investigation, which found that only Smith, Warner, and Bancroft knew of the plot. Meanwhile, former head coach Darren Lehmann denied that knowledge of the scheme was widespread throughout the wider team.

stories.title: Loud Booms Resound Across Riyadh Following Civil Defence Threat Alert
stories.summary:
Several loud explosions echoed through the Saudi capital of Riyadh on Sunday shortly after the Civil Defence issued an early-warning alert regarding a potential security threat. Authorities subsequently confirmed that the immediate danger had passed, following a series of regional escalations involving Yemen's Houthi movement.

Earlier on Sunday, Saudi Arabia's air defence systems intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile targeted at the kingdom's eastern region. Coalition spokesperson Brig. Gen. Turki al-Maliki confirmed that the projectile was successfully neutralized before reaching the Eastern Province, while the Civil Defence Directorate activated warning systems across Dammam, Al-Ahsa, and Abqaiq.

Tensions have intensified following a surge in fighting that shattered a 2022 United Nations-brokered truce. Houthi-run media reported that recent Saudi airstrikes on Bani Hushaysh near Sanaa resulted in 33 deaths and 39 injuries, predominantly among women and children, though Saudi officials stated they were investigating the claims.

Concurrently, Yemeni government forces announced they had executed 875 military operations under Operation Dawn of Yemen, claiming to have neutralized 130 Houthi fighters and commanders. Ground and air clashes persisted across Taiz, Marib, and Al-Jawf provinces as both sides continued hostile military maneuvers.

stories.title: راولپنڈی پولیس کی کارروائیاں، رواں سال 1804 منشیات سپلائرز گرفتار
stories.summary:
راولپنڈی پولیس نے رواں سال کے پہلے دس ماہ کے دوران منشیات کے خلاف موثر کارروائیاں کرتے ہوئے مجموعی طور پر 1786 مقدمات درج کیے۔ ان کارروائیوں کے نتیجے میں 1804 منشیات سپلائرز کو حتحراست میں لیا گیا۔

پولیس ترجمان کے مطابق، گرفتار کیے جانے والے منشیات فروشوں کے قبضے سے کروڑوں روپے مالیت کی منشیات برآمد کی گئی ہے۔ اس برآمدگی میں ایک ٹن 287 کلوگرام یعنی 1288.613 کلو سے زائد چرس، ساڑھے چھ کلو سے زائد ہیروئن، ساڑھے سترہ کلو سے زیادہ آئس اور 10744 لیٹر شراب شامل ہے۔

پولیس حکام کا عزم ہے کہ معاشرے سے منشیات کے ناسور کو جڑ سے ختم کرنے کے لیے تمام ضروری اقدامات کیے جا رہے ہیں۔ راولپنڈی پولیس شہریوں کو ایک پرامن اور محفوظ ماحول فراہم کرنے کے لیے ہمہ وقت مصروف عمل ہے۔

stories.title: پولینڈ کے شہر کراکو میں فائرنگ سے 6 افراد ہلاک اور 15 زخمی
stories.summary:
یورپی ملک پولینڈ کے تاریخی شہر کراکو کے مصروف ترین سیاحتی مقام پر ایک مسلح شخص نے گاڑی میں سوار ہو کر اندھا دھند گولیاں برسا دیں۔ اس اندحے تشدد کے نتیجے میں 6 افراد ہلاک جبکہ 15 زخمی ہو گئے۔

خبر رساں اداروں ایسوسی ایٹڈ پریس اور رائٹرز کے مطابق یہ ہولناک واقعہ سہ پہر تقریباً 3 بجے شہر کے مین مارکیٹ اسکوائر میں پیش آیا، جہاں سیاحوں اور مقامی شہریوں کی بہت بڑی تعداد موجود تھی۔ حملہ آور نے مرکزی چوک میں گاڑی چلاتے ہوئے مختلف مقامات پر لوگوں کو نشانہ بنایا۔

اچانک فائرنگ کی آوازیں گونجنے پر علاقے میں شدید بھگدڑ مچ گئی اور خوفزدہ شہری اپنی جانیں بچانے کے لیے قریبی دکانوں اور عمارتوں کے اندر چھپ گئے۔ پولیس نے فوری جوابی کارروائی کرتے ہوئے ملزم کو زخمی حالت میں گرفتار کر لیا۔

stories.title: Pakistani TV Dramas Balance Social Themes with Commercial and Patriarchal Pressures
stories.summary:
Television programming in Pakistan is a multi-billion-rupee industry heavily driven by corporate advertising and conservative norms. Networks favor predictable storylines to guarantee return on investment, while experimental content faces strict internal review boards and state regulatory bodies. These entities often prefer idealized traditionalism over uncomfortable realities, ensuring that prime-time slots remain safe for family audiences and corporate product placements. Consequently, television ratings consistently take precedence over artistic bravery.

Despite this cautious environment, a current prime-time drama has achieved massive viewership and sparked widespread national discussion by touching upon mental health struggles, emotional gaslighting, and panic attacks. The storyline follows an ambitious young woman whose plans to study abroad are derailed by a manipulative ex-boyfriend who abandons her under the guise of religious awakening. Left behind to face social isolation and clinical depression, the protagonist struggles to recover from the trauma caused by the toxic relationship.

However, the drama's narrative path ultimately reverts to traditional, regressive tropes. Rather than portraying female agency, financial independence, or professional psychiatric help, the protagonist's emotional rehabilitation is tied directly to a new male lead. This righteous and soft-spoken character acts as a classic savior figure, and the narrative implies her severe panic attacks can be cured through his presence and spiritually blessed water. By framing her recovery around male protection, the show reinforces patriarchal stereotypes.

Behind these plots are screenwriters who must navigate the demanding pressures of Television Rating Points (TRPs) and advertising revenue. While writers may wish to introduce intellectual depth and complex themes, network executives frequently demand emotional catharsis and recognizable relationship dynamics. To succeed commercially, writers often utilize familiar family drama frameworks to introduce subtle social issues, ultimately resulting in narratives that appease both corporate employers and conservative audiences by conforming to expected societal norms.

stories.title: Digital Algorithms Shape Children's Interests and Challenge Parents
stories.summary:
Parents today face a growing challenge in monitoring what their young children watch online, as algorithmic recommendation systems constantly suggest new videos, toys, and behaviors. Unlike traditional scheduled television, video platforms serve an endless stream of content based on past viewing habits, creating an echo chamber that can rapidly influence a child's preferences, accents, and demands.

For 34-year-old Sidrah Khan, whose seven-year-old daughter watches YouTube vlogs, filtering out unsuitable or inaccessible lifestyle content has proven difficult. Despite efforts to select educational shows, subsequent video recommendations often leave a lasting impression. Similarly, Farwa Naqvi noted that while programs like Ms Rachel and Pakkay Dost aided her three-year-old son's language development, unchosen cartoon recommendations led to hyperactivity, and blocking channels failed to stop similar content from appearing.

This digital exposure is increasingly visible in classrooms. Erum Muhammad Ayub, a junior and computing teacher at a private school, observes that students frequently bring online trends and shared gaming interests, such as Roblox, into their daily school activities.

While recommendation algorithms can introduce children to positive educational subjects like science and languages, experts like social media analyst Kamran Karim point out that repetition narrows the variety of content children encounter. This rapid and frequent exposure leaves parents struggling to maintain control over their developing children's interests and habits.

stories.title: The Modern Obsession with Scheduling Personal Rest and Solitude
stories.summary:
In contemporary society, leisure has shifted from simply having nothing to do into a carefully planned necessity requiring strict boundaries. People now schedule downtime, protect quiet hours, and carve out "me time" to cope with constant digital notifications, work demands, and the pressures of being perpetually reachable. This need for solitude has spawned books, podcasts, and entire self-care industries dedicated to mental wellbeing.

This modern retreat into privacy is driven by the reality of continuous connectivity, where phones, work emails, and social media keep the outside world constantly intrusive. For many, like 60-year-old university employee Fariha, socialising requires emotional effort after a long day, making an evening switch-off routine a vital shield against exhaustion. Similarly, 36-year-old accountant and mother Ayesha must carefully engineer alone time after managing the heavy demands of work and family life.

Psychologists emphasize that these periods of solitude are essential for mental maintenance. Dr. Muhammad Hamza Atiq, a senior instructor in psychiatry at AKUH, explains that the mind requires breaks from continuous engagement to regulate emotions, recover attention, and process experiences.

However, experts caution that healthy boundaries must not turn into total isolation. While choosing solitude to recharge is beneficial, withdrawing completely from relationships is counterproductive. The ultimate goal is to maintain enough personal autonomy and rest to comfortably handle the daily interruptions of life.

stories.title: Solar Power Expansion Faces Infrastructure and Cost Hurdles in Gilgit-Baltistan
stories.summary:
Gilgit-Baltistan faces severe energy challenges as climate-induced disasters repeatedly disrupt its electricity supplies. Intense rains in 2025 triggered landslides that caused massive financial losses exceeding Rs20 billion, damaging both main hydropower infrastructure and alternative transport routes. For truck driver Muhammad Anwar, a landslide on the Karakoram Highway left his delivery of government solar panels stranded while his home remained without light at night.

To combat regular winter outages and grid failures, the federal government allocated 58 MW of solar capacity in March 2026, alongside a separate 100 MW solarisation initiative aimed at reaching nearly 148,000 households with free solar panels. However, out of 15,733 households selected through balloting, 3,725 left their units in warehouses because the panels alone are insufficient. Beneficiaries must independently purchase costly components like batteries, inverters, and mounting structures, adding between Rs90,000 and over Rs180,000 in expenses—a prohibitive sum for families relying on the subsidy.

Despite financial and logistical hurdles, solar technology is transforming various sectors across the region. Initiatives by organizations like AKRSP, UNDP, and WWF have introduced solar lift irrigation systems to help farmers draw water from distant rivers, and over 500 passive solar greenhouses allow year-round vegetable cultivation. Additionally, solar power with battery storage enables local businesses, such as a women-led fitness studio in Skardu, to maintain evening operations during power cuts.

While complete solar systems provide reliable light for studying and daily chores, bridging the gap between receiving a free panel and affording a functional system remains a significant hurdle for low-income households in the region.

stories.title: Trump's Coalition Collapses Following Economic Strain and Foreign Policy Crises
stories.summary:
A historic "blue wave" swept the United States in a post-election shift, resulting in Democrats flipping key Senate seats in Texas, South Carolina, and Kansas, while securing a major congressional victory. Veteran journalist Storer Rowley and analyses from the New York Times attributed this seismic political shift to a complete collapse of the Republican coalition, driven by massive swings among young and Hispanic voters who previously supported Donald Trump.

Trump’s defeat was heavily fueled by domestic economic hardship and controversial foreign policy decisions. Having campaigned as an anti-war candidate, Trump initiated a conflict with Iran that closed the Strait of Hormuz, drove gas prices past $4 a gallon, and pushed inflation to 3.7 percent. Rowley criticized the administration for failing to lower prices, compounding costs through tariffs, and engaging in corruption that allegedly enriched Trump and his family by billions of dollars during his second term.

International relations expert Ashok Swain noted that the Republican setback reflects deep global unease with Trump's authoritarian style, disregard for democratic institutions, and unyielding support for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Swain warned that while the election results signal declining public support for the war in Iran, a politically weakened Trump might still act unilaterally or escalate conflicts to project domestic strength.

With Democrats capturing control of both chambers of Congress, lawmakers face immediate opportunities to investigate military operations, scrutinize arms sales, and challenge ongoing foreign military engagements. However, Swain cautioned that the American presidency retains vast unilateral foreign-policy powers, meaning congressional oversight will face distinct structural limits.

stories.title: Carlos Alcaraz Advances to Paris Masters Final After Defeating Casper Ruud
stories.summary:
Spanish tennis star Carlos Alcaraz advanced to the Paris Masters final following a straight-sets victory over Norway's Casper Ruud at the Plenitude Arena in Nanterre on November 7, 2026. The second-seeded Alcaraz secured a controlled 6-4, 6-4 win, breaking Ruud in the seventh game of the first set and sealing the match with an ace on his second attempt during the second set. This victory sets up a title clash with American player Ben Shelton, who earned his spot by defeating French world number 47 Luca Van Assche 5-7, 6-3, 6-4.

Reflecting on the upcoming match, Alcaraz noted that facing Shelton is one of the premier challenges in tennis, recalling their previous meeting when Shelton eliminated him in the US Open quarter-finals earlier in the season. Alcaraz emphasized that his reflexes must be at peak performance to return Shelton's powerful serves, while expressing delight at finally reaching his first Paris Masters final after previously suffering painful early-round exits at the tournament.

Meanwhile, Shelton advanced to his sixth final of the season and aims for his third Masters-level title, having won the previous two editions of the Canadian Open. The left-hander overcame a first-set loss against Van Assche by raising his level in the subsequent sets, ultimately breaking his opponent in the decider to secure victory. Shelton credited his enjoyment on the court for keeping him engaged at this late stage of the season.

For Alcaraz, reaching the final marks a significant milestone after grinding down opponents from the baseline throughout the week. The Spaniard entered the semi-finals following an exhilarating comeback win over Taylor Fritz in the previous round, whereas his opponent Ruud exited after a solid run. Sunday's final promises an intense encounter between two of the sport's top competitors at the Parisian venue.

stories.title: UAE Coast Guard Rescues 22 Arab Crew Members After Cargo Ship Fire
stories.summary:
The United Arab Emirates National Guard announced that its Coast Guard Group successfully rescued 22 Arab nationals after a fire erupted aboard a cargo ship in the Sea of Oman. Specialized teams were dispatched immediately following a distress call from the vessel's crew, locating the ship and safely evacuating all personnel.

All rescued crew members received necessary first aid and were reported to be in stable condition upon being transferred to appropriate authorities. The UAE National Guard highlighted the operation as evidence of its rapid response capabilities and ongoing commitment to maritime security and the preservation of human life in regional waters.

In separate regional maritime incidents, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy claimed that two oil tankers suffered severe damage after striking sea mines near the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC alleged that both vessels had deactivated their navigation systems and attempted to traverse unauthorized routes.

Additionally, US Central Command reported that military forces disabled a St. Kitts-flagged commercial vessel, the M/V Huda, in the Gulf of Oman after its crew ignored warnings and attempted to breach the American naval blockade against Iran. CENTCOM noted that the strike was executed using precision munitions fired from a military aircraft.

stories.title: افغان وزیر داخلہ کے ذاتی محافظ دند غوری میں قتل
stories.summary:
افغانستان کے عبوری وزیر داخلہ سراج الدین حقانی کے ذاتی محافظ کو صوبہ بغلان میں نامعلوم مسلح افراد کی فائرنگ کے نتیجے میں قتل کر دیا گیا۔ مقتول کی گولیاں لگی ہوئی لاش ضلع دند غوری میں سڑک کے کنارے سے برآمد ہوئی۔

افغان میڈیا اور مقامی ذرائع کے مطابق یہ پُراسرار واقعہ جمعہ چھ نومبر دو ہزار چھبیس کو پیش آیا تھا۔ ہفتے کے روز اس واقعے کی تصدیق سامنے آئی اور مقتول کی شناخت بھی ظاہر کی گئی جو کہ سراج الدین حقانی کے قریبی حلقوں سے تعلق رکھتے تھے۔

مارے جانے والے محافظ کا نام قاری نور جان احمدزئی تھا جو اپنے عرفی نام 'طیب بدری' سے بھی پہچانے جاتے تھے۔ ان کا اصل تعلق صوبہ بغلان کے اسی ضلع دند غوری سے تھا جہاں انہیں نشانہ بنایا گیا۔

مقامی ذرائع کے مطابق قاری نور جان اپنے اہلخانہ سے ملاقات کی غرض سے اپنے آبائی علاقے آئے ہوئے تھے۔ اسی دوران نامعلوم ملزمان نے انہیں فائرنگ کر کے موت کے گھاٹ اتار دیا اور لاش سڑک کنارے چھوڑ کر فرار ہو گئے۔

stories.title: گوجرانوالہ اور ساہیوال میں ضمنی انتخابات، مختلف سیاسی اور انتظامی امور پر اہم خبریں
stories.summary:
گوجرانوالہ کے حلقے این اے 77 اور ساہیوال کے حلقے پی پی 203 میں ضمنی انتخاب کے لیے پولنگ کا سامان اور سیکیورٹی کے تمام انتظامات مکمل کر لیے گئے ہیں۔ یاد رہے کہ این اے 77 کی نشست مسلم لیگ ن کے رہنما محمود بشیر ورک اور پی پی 203 کی نشست حنیف جٹ کے انتقال کی وجہ سے خالی ہوئی تھی۔ انتخابی مہم کے دوران ضابطۂ اخلاق کی خلاف ورزی پر وفاقی وزیر اطلاعات عطاء اللّٰہ تارڑ کو نوٹس جاری کیا گیا ہے اور الیکشن کمیشن نے انہیں وضاحت کے لیے طلب کیا ہے۔

اس کے علاوہ ملک بھر سے دیگر اہم خبریں بھی سامنے آئی ہیں۔ پولیس نے قصور کے علاقے میں ایک بچے کو بدفعلی کے بعد قتل کرنے والے ملزم کو گرفتار کر لیا ہے۔ پشاور ہائی کورٹ نے گورنر راج اور سابق وزیراعلیٰ کی گرفتاری سے متعلق درخواستیں 10 نومبر کی کاز لسٹ سے ہٹا دی ہیں۔ وفاقی وزیر موسمیاتی تبدیلی مصدق ملک نے متوسط طبقے کی گاڑیوں پر ٹیکس کا بوجھ کم کرنے کی ضرورت پر زور دیا ہے۔

وفاقی تحقیقاتی ادارے ایف آئی اے نے نادرا کے ایک سابق اسسٹنٹ ڈائریکٹر کو گرفتار کیا ہے۔ گورنر خیبرپختونخوا فیصل کریم کنڈی نے کہا ہے کہ ریاست کے خلاف جنگ کرنے والوں کے خلاف سخت کارروائی ہوگی۔ اسلام آباد میں مشکوک الیکٹرانک ڈیوائسز ملنے پر چار پیٹرول پمپس کے خلاف مقدمات درج کر لیے گئے ہیں جبکہ کراچی ساؤتھ پولیس نے لودھراں سے کراچی لائی جانے والی دو لڑکیوں کو بازیاب کرا لیا ہے۔

ان تمام واقعات اور حکومتی اقدامات کا مقصد ملک بھر میں امن و امان کی بحالی، انتظامی امور کی بہتری اور انتخابی عمل کو شفاف بنانا ہے۔ مختلف محکمے اور قانون نافذ کرنے والے ادارے ان معاملات کی مزید تحقیقات اور قانونی کارروائی میں مصروف عمل ہیں۔

stories.title: اسلام آباد میں پاکستان منرلز انویسٹمنٹ فورم کا انعقاد بارہ نومبر کو ہوگا
stories.summary:
پاکستان اپنے وسیع معدنی ذخائر سے بھرپور فائدہ اٹھانے کے لیے عالمی کمپنیوں کی میزبانی اور غیر ملکی سرمایہ کاری کے استقبال کی مکمل تیاری کر چکا ہے۔ اسی سلسلے میں پاکستان منرلز انویسٹمنٹ فورم بارہ اور تیرہ نومبر کو اسلام آباد میں منعقد کیا جا رہا ہے۔

معدنی شعبے میں سرمایہ کاری کو فروغ دینے والا یہ اہم فورم اسپیشل انویسٹمنٹ فیسیلیٹیشن کونسل کے تعاون سے منعقد ہو رہا ہے۔ اس دو روزہ تقریب میں ملک کی سیاسی و عسکری قیادت کے ساتھ ساتھ عالمی مائننگ ایگزیکٹوز، بڑے سرمایہ کار، پالیسی ساز اور شعبے کے ماہرین شرکت کریں گے۔

فورم کے دوران معدنیات اور کان کنی کی ویلیو چین سے متعلقہ مختلف کمپنیوں، منصوبوں، مصنوعات، خدمات، سامان اور جدید ٹیکنالوجیز کی نمائش کا اہتمام بھی کیا جائے گا۔ اس کا بنیادی مقصد ملک کے قیمتی معدنی وسائل کو بروئے کار لاتے ہوئے اندرونی اور بیرونی سرمایہ کاری کی راہ ہموار کرنا ہے۔

پاکستان منرل انویسٹمنٹ فورم کے صدر احمد حیات لک نے تمام متعلقہ شخصیات اور عالمی رہنماؤں کو اس میں شرکت کی دعوت دی ہے۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ یہ فورم عالمی تکنیکی شراکت داری، پالیسی اصلاحات اور پائیدار مائننگ کے لیے نئے دروازے کھولے گا۔

stories.title: AS Roma Moves Second in Serie A with 3-0 Victory Over Sassuolo
stories.summary:
AS Roma climbed to second place in the Serie A standings after securing a 3-0 victory over Sassuolo at the Stadio Olimpico on Saturday. Maintaining their unbeaten start to the season, Roma reached 27 points, putting them one point behind league leaders Lazio and two points ahead of third-placed Inter Milan. The defeat left struggling Sassuolo just above the relegation zone after conceding 29 goals across 11 league matches.

The deadlock was broken in the 27th minute when Roma defender Mario Hermoso capitalized on a loose ball following an intercepted pass and fired a shot into the roof of the net. Just three minutes later, a strike from Donyell Malen deflected off a Sassuolo defender before Sebastian Walukiewicz inadvertently turned the ball into his own goal. Despite several saves from Sassuolo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric, Rodrigo Mora sealed the victory for the hosts with a 58th-minute goal.

Dutch striker Donyell Malen has proven invaluable to manager Gian Piero Gasperini's squad, contributing eight league goals this campaign alongside four in the Champions League. Malen joined Roma on loan from Aston Villa in January and made his transfer permanent in May following a prolific run of form. Roma's high-scoring side has now tallied 31 goals in 11 matches, raising hopes for their first Scudetto since 2001.

In other Serie A fixtures on Saturday, Bologna climbed to eighth place with a 2-1 victory over ten-man Parma, bringing their total to 17 points. Cagliari secured a narrow 1-0 win against Frosinone, while Torino and Lecce played to a 1-1 draw with both sides scoring via own goals. Action continues on Sunday with Lazio visiting Napoli and Inter hosting Como.

stories.title: Real Madrid Defeats Valencia 3-0 to Draw Level with Barcelona
stories.summary:
Real Madrid secured an eighth consecutive victory across all competitions by defeating 10-man Valencia 3-0 at the Mestalla Stadium on Saturday. The win puts manager Jose Mourinho’s side provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona. Federico Valverde opened the scoring with a drilled shot from outside the area, and Arda Guler quickly doubled the lead before halftime. Kylian Mbappe added a third in the second half, marking his seventh consecutive match with a goal and his 13th league strike of the campaign.

The match was played without Real winger Vinicius Junior, who was serving the final game of a four-match suspension. Early in the encounter, players and fans paused in the ninth minute to pay tribute to the late Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel. Valencia struggled to find a foothold despite a disallowed goal by Guido Rodriguez and a smart save by Real goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois against Aaron Mayol. The hosts' evening worsened when captain Jose Gaya was dismissed late in the game for a sliding foul on Mbappe.

Mourinho praised his squad's emotional balance following their previous defeat to Atletico Madrid on September 20, noting that the team had maintained their composure and understood the reasons for that setback. Real Madrid have thrived despite their absences, maintaining heavy pressure on Barcelona at the top of the table. Meanwhile, Valencia remains 19th in the standings, sitting just one point away from the safety zone.

In other La Liga fixtures, new Espanyol coach Eder Sarabia oversaw a goalless home draw against Deportivo La Coruna. Osasuna claimed a late 1-1 draw against Athletic Bilbao, and Racing Santander came from behind to defeat Malaga 2-1. Barcelona's subsequent match against Atletico Madrid was scheduled for Sunday.

stories.title: غزہ میں شدید بارشوں سے خیمہ بستیاں زیرِ آب، ہزاروں بے گھر افراد متاثر
stories.summary:
غزہ میں سرد موسم کی پہلی شدید بارش نے اسرائیلی کارروائیوں کے سبب بے گھر ہونے والے فلسطینی خاندانوں کی تکالیف میں نمایاں اضافہ کر دیا ہے۔ موسلادھار بارش کے نتیجے میں خطے کے مختلف حصوں میں قائم خیمہ بستیاں پانی میں ڈوب گئیں، جس کی وجہ سے ہزاروں خاندانوں کا ذاتی سامان، بستر، کمبل اور گدے مکمل طور پر بھیگ گئے اور متعدد عارضی پناہ گاہیں رہائش کے قابل نہیں رہیں۔

گزشتہ بارہ گھنٹوں کے دوران تقریباً ستر ہزار خیمے بارش کے پانی سے براہِ راست متاثر ہوئے ہیں۔ اس ناگہانی صورتحال نے دسیوں ہزار بے گھر فلسطینیوں کو انتہائی کٹھن حالات سے دوچار کر دیا ہے، جن میں بڑی تعداد خواتین، بچوں، معمر افراد اور بیمار مریضوں کی پر مشتمل ہے۔

غزہ کی سول ڈیفنس سروس کے اعداد و شمار کے مطابق، بارش کا سلسلہ شروع ہونے کے محض دس گھنٹوں کے اندر اندر شہریوں کی طرف سے مدد طلب کرنے کے لیے لگ بھگ پندرہ سو ہنگامی کالز موصول ہوئیں۔

کئی مقامات پر پانی کا بہاؤ تیس سے چالیس سینٹی میٹر تک بلند ریکارڈ کیا گیا، جس کی وجہ سے خیموں اور عارضی کیمپوں میں رہنے والے مکینوں کو مجبوراََ محفوظ مقامات کی طرف ہجرت کرنا پڑی۔

stories.title: Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund Win to Maintain Bundesliga Lead
stories.summary:
Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund both secured 2-1 victories on Saturday to remain neck and neck at the top of the German Bundesliga table. Bayern defeated Mainz away at the MEWA Arena, while Dortmund overcame Elversberg at Signal Iduna Park. Both clubs are locked on 21 points after nine rounds of matches, with defending champions Bayern holding the top spot on goal difference. Phillip Tietz scored a stoppage-time goal for Mainz, but it came too late to prevent Bayern from claiming only their third win in their last seven visits to the venue.

Bayern played without manager Vincent Kompany, who was recovering from illness, alongside a long absentee list that included Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari, and Serge Gnabry. Joshua Kimmich opened the scoring after 14 minutes, reacting emotionally following bereavement leave after his father's death. Harry Kane, who recently extended his contract until 2029, provided the assist for Kimmich and later set up Lennart Karl for the second goal. Manuel Neuer set a club record by appearing at 40 years and 225 days old, though he was substituted before halftime due to a foot injury. Dortmund secured their victory thanks to a second-half brace from Felix Nmecha, despite a late goal from Noel Futkeu.

In other matches, VfB Stuttgart defeated Werder Bremen 1-0 via an early Maximilian Mittelstaedt goal, while RB Leipzig recovered from conceding in the opening minute to beat Augsburg 5-2, moving into third place. Eintracht Frankfurt drew 2-2 with promoted Paderborn after Jonathan Burkardt scored twice.

The results leave the top of the Bundesliga tightly contested as teams head toward the international break. Bayern and Dortmund continue to set the pace despite various squad challenges and injuries.

stories.title: PSG Extends Winning Streak to Eleven Matches with Victory Over Troyes
stories.summary:
Paris Saint-Germain claimed an unspectacular 1-0 victory over Troyes at the Parc des Princes on Saturday, extending their winning streak to 11 consecutive matches across all competitions. Ukraine defender Illia Zabarnyi scored the game's only goal in the 39th minute, heading in a cross from Senny Mayulu following a quickly taken corner by Desire Doue. The win moves Luis Enrique's side three points clear at the top of the French Ligue 1 table, with seven consecutive league wins under their belt.

PSG played the fixture without several key players, including injured stars Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembele, Nuno Mendes, Maghnes Akliouche, and captain Marquinhos, while Achraf Hakimi was rested and Joao Neves started on the bench. Despite dominating possession, forward Ferran Torres missed multiple scoring opportunities, continuing a drought that has stretched to eight games without a goal. Troyes, backed by the City Football Group and fighting against relegation, threatened through Renaud Ripart and Lucas Maronnier, whose late effort was ruled out for offside.

Manager Luis Enrique expressed satisfaction with the team's consistency, particularly praising their performances since the previous international break. The victory provides PSG with momentum ahead of their upcoming fixture against Nice and a scheduled Champions League match against AS Roma.

In earlier action, neighbor club Paris FC secured a 1-0 away victory against Auxerre thanks to a second-half goal by Lassine Sinayoko, keeping them in second place. Other matches saw Lille, Lyon, Lens, and Marseille scheduled to play on Sunday.

stories.title: Manchester City Suffers Third Straight Loss as Arsenal Extends Lead
stories.summary:
Manchester City fell to a third consecutive Premier League defeat on Saturday, losing 3-1 away to Nottingham Forest at the City Ground. The result allowed Arsenal to stretch their lead at the top of the table to six points. Forest established a two-goal lead by the 18th minute through goals from Jair Cunha and Liam Delap. Although City improved in the second half and pulled a goal back through Rayan Cherki, Delap restored Forest's two-goal advantage in the 73rd minute to seal the victory for Oliver Glasner's side.

City manager Enzo Maresca admitted his team failed to match Forest's intensity in the opening half, emphasizing the need for balance after a strong start to the season that included seven consecutive league wins. City currently face significant off-field pressure as they await the outcome of more than 100 alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules. Meanwhile, Forest celebrated a historic home performance that lifted them away from the relegation zone.

Arsenal strengthened their position at the summit by overcoming Hull City 1-0 at the Emirates Stadium. Captain Martin Odegaard broke the deadlock in the 72nd minute, following up after goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled a shot from Noni Madueke. Manager Mikel Arteta praised the result but stressed the importance of converting chances to avoid tense finishes.

In other fixtures, Leeds United defeated Tottenham Hotspur 1-0 with a late goal from substitute Noah Okafor, ending Tottenham's three-match winning streak. Newcastle United drew 1-1 with Fulham after Rodrigo Muniz cancelled out Jacob Murphy's opening strike. The results left Michael Carrick's Manchester United entering Sunday's fixture against Aston Villa inside the relegation zone.

stories.title: کراچی کے ساحلِ سمندر سی ویو پر ڈائیننگ یوتھ رن ریس کا انعقاد
stories.summary:
کراچی کے ساحلِ سمندر سی ویو پر ڈائیننگ یوتھ رن ریس کا انعقاد کیا گیا جس میں شہر بھر کے نوجوانوں نے بھرپور انداز میں شرکت کی۔ پانچ کلومیٹر طویل اس دوڑ کے مقابلے میں نوجوان لڑکوں اور لڑکیوں کی بڑی تعداد موجود تھی، جن کے لیے مقابلے کی الگ الگ کیٹیگریز رکھی گئی تھیں۔

منتظمین کے مطابق اس ریس میں ایک ہزار سے زائد نوجوان لڑکوں اور پانچ سو سے زیادہ لڑکیوں نے حصہ لیا۔ اس ایونٹ کا بنیادی مقصد نوجوان طبقے کو صحت مند سرگرمیوں کی جانب مائل کرنا، معاشرے میں کھیلوں کے رجحان کو فروغ دینا اور شرکا کو جسمانی فٹنس کی اہمیت سے آگاہ کرنا تھا۔

مقابلے کے اختتام پر شاندار کارکردگی کا مظاہرہ کرنے والے کامیاب شرکا میں حوصلہ افزائی کے لیے سرٹیفکیٹس اور نقد انعامات تقسیم کیے گئے۔ اس نوعیت کی تقریبات کا انعقاد نوجوانوں میں مثبت توانائی اجاگر کرنے اور انہیں صحت مندانہ تفریح فراہم کرنے کے لیے اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے۔

stories.title: Islamabad High Court Reserves Judgment on FBR Production Monitoring System
stories.summary:
The Islamabad High Court has reserved its decision regarding numerous constitutional petitions that challenge the Federal Board of Revenue’s electronic production monitoring system. A division bench composed of Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro and Justice Umair Malik presided over the hearings involving over 300 industrial units from sectors such as textiles, beverages, cooking oil, packaged milk, and food processing.

The contesting industrial units challenged the constitutional validity and legality of the production monitoring mechanism introduced under Section 40C of the Sales Tax Act, 1990. Petitioners argued that the FBR lacks the proper authority to install electronic monitoring devices on their premises, raised concerns about the financial expenses tied to the equipment, and claimed the system disrupts their regular business operations.

Govenerment counsel Hafiz Ehsaan Ahmad Khokhar defended the statutory authority and legislative competence behind Section 40C. He explained that the provision was enacted in 2013 to enhance the tracking of industrial production, sales, and stocks while curbing tax evasion. Khokhar detailed that the framework relies on specific subsections and Chapter XIV-BA of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006, which govern video analytics and digital-eye technology.

Khokhar noted that similar monitoring systems are already active in major sectors like tobacco, sugar, cement, and fertilizer without prior judicial intervention. He argued that expanding the mechanism ensures verified production, prevents under-invoicing, and promotes a fair marketplace. Following the detailed arguments presented by both sides, the bench officially reserved its judgment.

stories.title: PHDEC and GPI Collaborate to Expand Balochistan Horticultural Exports
stories.summary:
Muhammad Naseer, CEO of the Pakistan Horticulture Development and Export Company, visited the Green Pakistan Initiative head office on October 29, 2026. During the visit, project director Asif Khan briefed officials on the horticultural processing and storage infrastructure currently under development across Balochistan to boost regional agricultural exports.

The infrastructure project spans 22 locations across 20 districts, targeting major fruits and vegetables such as apples, dates, tomatoes, onions, pomegranates, grapes, plums, and cherries. Each designated location features a cold storage capacity of 1,000 tonnes alongside processing rates ranging from 1 to 5 tonnes per hour. Eight of these facilities are slated to begin operations in the coming months.

Naseer praised the initiative for strengthening horticultural value chains and supporting traceable, commercial-scale production. He suggested prioritizing items like date paste, date syrup, dried onions, tomato pulp, and apple cider for export through partnerships with local traders. Khan endorsed the recommendations and confirmed participation in the upcoming FoodAg exhibition.

The GPI plans to display its value-added goods at the FoodAg event, scheduled for November 23–26 in Karachi. This engagement aims to connect international buyers with Pakistan's horticultural output, while Naseer reaffirmed PHDEC's dedication to improving market access for regional producers.

stories.title: UN Women Pakistan Recognizes 17 Honorees at 2026 WEPs Awards
stories.summary:
The biennial Women’s Empowerment Principles Awards in Pakistan recently celebrated 17 winners and runner-up recipients across seven distinct categories. Selected from a pool of 52 nationwide applicants ranging from small enterprises to large corporations, the honorees were recognized for advancing gender equality throughout their respective business value chains.

The 2026 awards ceremony was hosted by UN Women Pakistan in collaboration with Derien, Soorty, and media partner GEO. Jamshed M Kazi, the UN Women Pakistan Country Representative, emphasized that true business success involves transforming lives and removing barriers for female leadership. Syed Nasir Hussain Shah, Minister for Local Government and chief guest at the event, noted that women's economic participation remains essential for the country's social and economic development.

Keynote speaker Nishat Fatima, CEO of South Air, stressed that empowering women drives organizational innovation and strengthens the economy. The event honored initiatives promoting inclusive workplaces, gender-responsive products, and inclusive procurement, highlighting the role of technology and small and medium-sized enterprises in fostering equal opportunities.

National winners from the Pakistan event will advance to the regional 2026 Asia-Pacific WEPs Awards, subject to final eligibility checks. The regional ceremony is scheduled to be broadcast on December 1, 2026. Globally, over 13,400 companies participate in the WEPs directory, with more than 190 companies representing Pakistan within the network.

stories.title: Sindh Food Authority Fines Karachi Cafe Rs200,000 Over Violations
stories.summary:
The Sindh Food Authority has penalized a cafe located in Karachi’s Defence area with a fine of Rs200,000 following routine health inspections. The penalty was issued after food safety officials discovered multiple expired items and strands of hair inside various food products at the establishment.
